## What The Midterm Measures

The midterm checks whether you can understand a short piece of code, identify
and repair an error, perform a small calculation, and explain what a result
does—and does not—establish. It combines ideas from several weeks rather than
asking you only to recall command names.

You will not need to write a long program from a blank page or produce essays.
Written answers may be a vector, a short calculation, a corrected line of code,
or a few sentences. Follow the response-length guidance in each question;
concise explanations and bullet points are acceptable.

## What To Review

Start with the material taught in class, the weekly survival checklists, and
the **core** exercises. The website is a resource bank: this guide is not an
instruction to complete every optional extension before the examination.

| Week | Revision focus | Materials |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Arrays, dimensions, indexing, matrix versus element-wise operations, plots, scripts, and numerical checks | [Week 1](../weeks/week-01.qmd) · [Exercises](../weeks/week-01-exercises.qmd) |
| 2 | Function inputs and outputs, conditions, logical selection, loops, debugging, and tests derived from a mathematical definition | [Week 2](../weeks/week-02.qmd) · [Exercises](../weeks/week-02-exercises.qmd) |
| 3 | Polynomial coefficients and evaluation, fitting, interpolation and extrapolation, residuals, RMSE, and separate fit/check observations | [Week 3](../weeks/week-03.qmd) · [Exercises](../weeks/week-03-exercises.qmd) |
| 4 | Numerical methods and their checks: roots, integration, optimization, and interpreting numerical results and visualizations | [Week 4](../weeks/week-04.qmd) · [Exercises](../weeks/week-04-exercises.qmd) |
| 5 | Symbolic versus numerical computation, exactness, assumptions and domains, differentiation, integration, solving equations, and optimization evidence | [Week 5](../weeks/week-05.qmd) · [Exercises](../weeks/week-05-exercises.qmd) |
| 6 | R vectors and data frames, indexing and logical selection, missing values, summaries, plot mappings and labels, and the source/render/output distinction in Quarto | [Week 6](../weeks/week-06.qmd) · [Exercises](../weeks/week-06-exercises.qmd) |

For Week 6, also review the difference between a descriptive association and a
causal claim. You are not expected to write a Quarto document from scratch.
Week 7 data-transformation material and later R topics are outside the scope.

## How To Prepare

1. **Try first, then check.** Revisit selected core exercises and lab starters.
   Make an attempt before opening the separately labelled possible solution.
   Explain any difference between your answer and the solution.
2. **Practise on paper.** Read a short code fragment without running it. Write
   the expected values, dimensions, or selected observations. Trace a loop one
   iteration at a time. Then use MATLAB or R to check your prediction during
   revision—not during the examination.
3. **Practise explanations as well as calculations.** For each result, ask:
   What was computed? What check supports it? What conclusion is justified?
   What remains uncertain? Do not use “the code runs” or “the plot looks right”
   as your only evidence.
4. **Use previous feedback.** Revisit the class discussion of Quiz 1, Quiz 2,
   and the exit tickets. The Quiz 2 practice activity in Blackboard can help
   with MATLAB reasoning, but it is not a complete midterm rehearsal: it does
   not cover Week 6 R or the full written format.
5. **Do a timed mixed practice session.** Choose several existing exercises
   across the six weeks. Work individually with only your handwritten sheet,
   without AI, software, or a calculator. Afterwards, identify whether errors
   came from notation, calculation, interpretation, or an inadequate check.

The [MATLAB recovery checkpoint](../weeks/recovery-after-week-05.qmd) and
[glossary](../resources/glossary.qmd) are available if you need to rebuild a
foundation before attempting mixed exercises.

## Preparing Your Handwritten Sheet

Organize the sheet around ideas you need to distinguish: representations,
operators, function contracts, validation checks, and MATLAB/R syntax. Include
brief reminders of what a check establishes and its limitations. Small examples
that you understand are more useful than pages of copied code.

The sheet must be **one A4 sheet handwritten by you**; both sides may be used.
Printed material, photocopies, and additional reference sheets are not allowed.

## Answering And Marking

- For each MCQ, select **one** answer. A correct single selection earns 2 marks;
  an incorrect, blank, or multiple selection earns 0. There is no negative
  marking and no written justification is required for an MCQ.
- Written questions allow partial credit for correct working and reasoning.
  Show the calculation or explanation requested; a bare answer may not earn
  full credit when justification is required.
- Equivalent correct code and mathematically correct explanations are accepted.
  Precise reasoning matters more than polished English or lengthy writing.
- Exact fractions and square roots are acceptable unless a question specifies
  otherwise. The arithmetic is intended to be manageable without a calculator.
- Use the suggested question timings as a guide and leave time to check your
  answers. If you use additional answer space, label the question and subpart.

## On The Day

Bring writing materials and your permitted handwritten sheet. Follow the room
and arrival instructions in Blackboard. Enter your name and student ID and
read and sign the academic integrity undertaking on the cover.

Work individually. AI, collaboration, unauthorized reference material, and
electronic devices are not permitted. Follow the invigilators' instructions
for storing phones, watches, and other devices. Keep the examination pages
together and return the complete paper, including any additional answer sheets.

Approved accommodations follow the usual course arrangements. If you cannot
attend, the [syllabus policy on missed
assessments](../syllabus/index.qmd#missed-assessments-and-late-project-submissions)
applies. Ask the instructor or TA before the examination if any preparation
instruction is unclear.

The live examination questions and answer key are not published on this site.
